claims.text: The United States moved to force the sale or ban of TikTok due to national security concerns, specifically regarding potential Chinese government access to US user data and the platform’s algorithm [Source: ev-1].

This concern was formalized in legislation signed by President Biden on 2024-04-24, which required ByteDance to divest TikTok's US operations within roughly 270 days (extendable by an additional 90 days) or face a ban [Source: ev-1].

Following a Supreme Court ruling that upheld the law with a vote of 9-0 on 2025-01-17, the app went dark in the US for approximately 14 hours around 2025-06-18/19 before being restored after President Trump pledged to pause enforcement [Source: ev-1].
An executive order issued on 2025-11-20 delayed enforcement for another 75 days [Source: ev-1].

The dispute was ultimately resolved through an Oracle-led deal announced on 2026-03-10, which granted Oracle about a 12.5% stake in TikTok's US operations while ByteDance retained majority interest [Source: ev-1].
This structure involved hosting US user data in Oracle’s cloud under US control (referred to as "Project Texas") and completing the final ownership structure by 2028 [Source: ev-1].
